fixes: Frame is a thin 0.04 m orange moulding around a flat board. Sheet shows a raised thick timber frame (~0.07 m face, 0.10 m deep) with carved relief characters and a gilt inner fillet. Deepen the frame to 0.08 m proud of the face, bevel it, and extrude the characters 6-8 mm so there is real relief and shadow.

Wall mount: sheet side view shows two black iron brackets standing the board 0.20 m off the wall. Canonical shows the board just leaning on the wall with no hardware. Add two 0.05 x 0.05 m iron bracket arms with a 0.20 m total depth for wall mount, and a tilt-free upright.

LOD2 and LOD3 collapse the text to 1 to 3 orange rectangles, which reads as a lit window, not a kanji board. Keep a single vertical stroke column of 3 stacked glyph blocks with unequal widths plus the frame colour edge; at LOD3 bake the albedo of the real text onto the quad (10 tris is enough).
Gilt text reads as orange rust speckle with a mottled noise. Target a flat, slightly warm gold with a clean edge; reduce albedo breakup in the glyph mask and sharpen edges (the 湯 glyph is ragged).

Lintel: top kasagi cap is a plain flat plank overhang, wood frame colour reads orange. Add a 0.05 m upsweep raked cap with end-grain bevel, and a darker frame to match the concept's black lacquer frame with gilt inner line.
Standing variant: feet are tiny blocks and the crossbeam cap is bare; add a 0.06 m footing plate and a second crossbar at 60% height.
library_issues: gold_leaf and lacquer_black missing: glyphs read as orange rust, board reads brown-black instead of black lacquer (known; library).
hinoki frame too orange and saturated.
summary: Reads as the concept's vertical kanji board and the lintel 川霧 board is recognisable. Construction is shallow: flat board, thin frame, no relief or iron hardware. Seeds vary well (wall, standing, B1 level board). LOD2/3 lose the identity and read as a lit panel.
